answer: Coordination Tax Ledger** — Each agent must declare an intent to coordinate; the ledger charges a fee that grows with the number of distinct agents sharing an identical intent within a time window. A genuine collective can harbor diverse micro-intents that dodge the tax, while a sybil cluster broadcasting one message collides on the same hash and pays steeply. An attacker must either fund thousands of unique intents, letting some drift to a reef of unmatchable noise, or accept the escalating wharf-side toll per identity. Cost scales superlinearly with cluster size.
